assumptions.description: The outcome $y_t\in\{0,1\}$ and prediction $p_t\in[0,1]$ are generated simultaneously each round. The outcome strategy may use all past predictions and outcomes, but not the realization of the current prediction or the current private seed.

structured_source_contract.timing: simultaneous choices; both may use past predictions/outcomes, adversary cannot see current realized randomized p_t before choosing y_t
structured_source_contract.bins: sum over exact prediction values actually used, not an independently fixed coarse histogram

operations.query_signature: The predictor chooses $p_t\in[0,1]$ while the adversary simultaneously chooses $y_t\in\{0,1\}$. Both may use past predictions and outcomes, but the adversary choosing $y_t$ cannot see the current realized randomized prediction $p_t$. After both act, $p_t,y_t$ is revealed. No true conditional mean or privileged prediction interface is supplied. Past feedback may be stored and reused computationally; no additional historical or sample queries are available beyond the explicitly declared interface.

source_fields.feasibility: Output a probability $p_t\in[0,1]$ each round. Evaluation uses the realized prediction and outcome trajectories; predictions cannot be rewritten after the game ends.
source_fields.allowed_postprocessing: Previously executed online actions cannot be changed.
source_fields.certificate_requirement: No function value, optimality certificate, or final recommendation is required unless explicitly listed for this axis.

source_fields.base_expression: $$\operatorname{Cal}_T=\sum_{p\in\{p_1,\ldots,p_T\}}\left|\sum_{t:p_t=p}(y_t-p_t)\right|.$$ Sum only over distinct forecast probabilities actually used. This is neither per-round absolute error nor binned approximate calibration.
source_fields.normalization: Group exactly equal prediction values and sum absolute deviations. Do not divide by T.
source_fields.finiteness_conditions: The triangle inequality places calibration error in $[0,T]$.

components.description: $T$ sequential rounds, or $T$ rounds per task

There are $T$ predictions and $N=T$ binary-outcome observations. Computation and observation counts are separate; information-theoretic existence does not imply an efficient algorithm. Initialization and exploration are charged. Information, arithmetic, communication, and memory remain separate resources; no optimal arithmetic or bit complexity is asserted.

view_override_policy.limitations: Mechanical merge does not certify consistency or mathematical identity. Narrative qualifications and source conditions remain authoritative.

source_fields.randomization: Private randomness is allowed and independent of the fixed instance and future external randomness.
source_fields.adaptivity: Strictly follows the per-round and within-batch protocol of the oracle
restrictions: Expectation includes both players' randomness; the target is neither a pathwise nor a high-probability calibration guarantee.

Private randomization is allowed, with the seed independent of the fixed instance and future external samples. Internal arithmetic, memory, linear spans, and iteration forms are unrestricted except for the stated computation, communication, privacy, and within-round interaction limits.
source_fields.internal_computation: Unrestricted except for explicit polynomial-time or protocol constraints
source_fields.parallelism: Follows the simultaneous-query, task-batch, and communication timing specified by the oracle

source_fields.complete_expression: Control $\mathbb E[\operatorname{Cal}_T]$ against every admissible outcome strategy, with expectation over both predictor and outcome-strategy randomness. Choose an admissible predictor first, then take the worst case over environment strategies.
aggregation_order: Control $\mathbb E[\operatorname{Cal}_T]$ against every admissible outcome strategy, with expectation over both predictor and outcome-strategy randomness. Choose an admissible predictor first, then take the worst case over environment strategies.
source_fields.quantifier_order: One admissible algorithm using only public information must handle every prescribed instance; adaptation to unknown budgets must be performed by that same algorithm.
randomness_sources: Observation or environment randomness explicitly allowed by the oracle.
source_fields.runtime_guarantee: The resource budget is fixed. Expected error is not automatically converted to high probability or a random-runtime bound.
